title: Diabetes emergencies in the hospital: DKA, HHS and hypoglycemia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's diabetes (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Diabetic ketoacidosis

Vitals:
BP: 138/82
HR: 88 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 96% on RA
Weight: 165 lbs

Recent Labs:
Glucose: 450 mg/dL (on admission)
BUN: 18 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 72 mL/min
pH: 7.22
Bicarb: 14 mEq/L
Ketones: Positive (urine)
HbA1c: 9.4%

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Fatigue, mild polyuria.
Respiratory: NAD.
CV: No chest pain, no SOB.
GI: Mild nausea, no vomiting.
Neuro: Alert and oriented x3.

Social History:
Retired. Lives with spouse. No tobacco use.

Family History:
Father: T2DM.
Mother: HTN.

Hospital Course:
Pt is a 90-year-old male with known T2DM admitted for DKA. Pt presented with signs of metabolic derangement. Initial management included aggressive IV fluid resuscitation and initiation of a continuous insulin drip. Patient responded well to treatment. Metabolic status stabilized; pH and bicarb improved significantly over 72 hours. Insulin drip was tapered and discontinued once patient was euvolumetric and ketone-negative. Transitioned to subcutaneous insulin regimen.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Diabetic ketoacidosis
- Type 2 diabetes

Discharge Medications:
- Insulin Glargine 20 units daily
- Insulin Lispro 5 units before meals
- Metformin 500mg BID

Follow-up:
F/u with primary care and endocrinology in 1 week for glucose monitoring and medication titration.

Electronically signed,
L. Moreau, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes with ketoacidosis without coma: E11.10 (HCC 36).

distractors.why: Ketoacidosis is a severe acute complication (HCC 36).
